# dte-sdk

> TypeScript SDK for Chilean electronic tax documents (DTE): build, stamp (TED), sign (XMLDSig) and envelope documents for the SII and talk to the SII web services (upload, status, acceptance/claims), with an English domain model, bilingual EN/ES JSDoc and RUT handling delegated to rut.ts.

The package has six entries, ES modules only, on Node ≥ 22.12 (`require()` loads them too): `dte-sdk` (documents, stamps, signatures, envelopes, books, the SII web services client over `fetch` and the public registry of authorized issuers; also runs on Bun and Deno and bundles for the browser), `dte-sdk/node` (`createNodeHttpsTransport`, `createDirectoryCapture`, `createDirectoryUploadArchive`, `createDirectoryTokenCache`, `createDirectoryFolioRegistry`, and the CAF file search `findCafFiles`, `findLatestCafFile`, `resolveCafFile`, `cafFileScope`, where the first three read a file that names no encoding, as the folio file the SII serves does, as UTF-8 when its bytes are and otherwise as ISO-8859-1, kept only if the SII's signature of the CAF read that way does not fail), `dte-sdk/portal` (the SII portal, folios, the register, the MIPYME backup, the activity verification, the certification sets and the certification runner), `dte-sdk/pdf` (printed samples and the SII office of each commune, `SII_OFFICES` and `siiOfficeForCommune`; needs the optional peers `pdf-lib` and `bwip-js`) and `dte-sdk/catalogs` (the SII's large code tables, apart so that only who imports them pays: the business activities, `BUSINESS_ACTIVITIES`, `businessActivity` and `isBusinessActivityCode`, and the customs tables of an export document, eight of Anexo 51 of the Compendio de Normas Aduaneras, `CUSTOMS_COUNTRIES`, `CUSTOMS_PORTS`, `CUSTOMS_TRANSPORT_ROUTES`, `CUSTOMS_SALE_CLAUSES`, `CUSTOMS_PAYMENT_TERMS`, `CUSTOMS_PACKAGE_TYPES`, `CUSTOMS_UNITS` and `CUSTOMS_SALE_MODES`, with `customsCode` and `customsName`; runs anywhere, like the root). `dte-sdk/schemas` holds the SII's schemas inside the package and validates a document against them: `validateAgainstSchema(xml, { schema })` returns `{ message, line }` issues, none when valid, by the schema of the document element (`schemaOf`) unless one is named (`DTE`, `EnvioDTE`, `EnvioBOLETA`, `LibroCV`, `LibroGuia`, `ConsumoFolio`, `RespuestaEnvioDTE`, `EnvioRecibos`, `AEC`; `SII_SCHEMAS`); its validator, `xmllint-wasm`, is an optional peer loaded on first use (`DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` without it); it is opt-in, checks structure alone, and nothing else in the package calls it. `DteError` and `isDteError` come from `dte-sdk` and recognize what every entry throws.

dte-sdk covers document types 33, 34, 39, 41, 43, 46, 52, 56 and 61, and the export documents 110, 111 and 112 (`isExport`). `createDocument` validates and normalizes input (RUTs via rut.ts, text sanitized, where `sanitizeText` writes a character outside ISO-8859-1 in the form it has there (`š` as `s`, `€` as `EUR`, a typographic dash as a hyphen), drops decoration such as an emoji, and refuses with `ENCODING_UNSUPPORTED_CHAR` a letter, a digit, a currency sign or a math sign that has no such form, schema lengths enforced, totals computed with per-line rounding, each line worked out exactly over its decimal digits and rounded half away from zero, each percent taken of the base already rounded to a whole peso (`calculateLineAmount`), after its quantity, price and percents are rounded the same way to the decimals their schema types hold, a global discount or surcharge in percent taken of its base the same way, a price with `unitPriceDecimals` written with them over its decimal digits, VAT-included prices via `MntBruto`, withholding for purchase invoices, receipt defaults). `totals.vatNotWithheld` writes `IVANoRet` (field 118) on a purchase invoice (46) and the notes that reference one; `splitVat` on a settlement invoice (43) writes the VAT of its commissions as the own VAT (`IVAProp`) and the rest as the third parties' (`IVATerc`); `options.payments` admits 30 installments (`INVALID_OPTION` past them); and a line of the document over 4,000 characters, as a header with many installments is, is broken again before signing, or refused with `FIELD_TOO_LONG` when it still does not fit. `transport` carries the transport of goods of a dispatch guide or an invoice that moves them, with the fields of Res. Ex. 144/2026 (`trailerLicensePlate`, `departureDate`, `departureTime`, `arrivalDate`), every one optional as `DTE_v10.xsd` declares it and checked before stamping; `options.transferType` takes 1 to 9, the values the schema admits, and is required on a dispatch guide (Formato DTE 2.5, field 7; `MISSING_FIELD`). The totals follow `IndExe`: `nonBillableAmount` (`MontoNF`, field 125) is the lines with `IndExe` 2 less the lines with `IndExe` 6, and may be negative; `depositGuarantee` (`GrntDep`, field 120) is the lines with `IndExe` 3, added to `totalAmount` (field 124), and only a 33, 34, 56 or 61 takes it: an `IndExe` 3 line on a 46 or 52 keeps its amount and is in no total, one on a 43 or an export document is `INVALID_OPTION` (dte-sdk's choice: the format's `IndExe` row admits the indicator there), and so is a `depositGuarantee` other than zero on any other type, a value that is not a number included (a given zero is none); lines with `IndExe` 4 or 5 are in no total, and an `IndExe` outside 1 to 6, `null` included, is `INVALID_OPTION`. `commissions` holds the commission and other charge lines of a settlement invoice (43), or of a purchase invoice and the notes that correct one: a line needs `netValue` or `exemptValue` (the one it lacks is written as zero, since the schema requires both), its `vatValue` defaults to its net value by the VAT rate, rounded, and the totals carry in `commissions` (`Totales/Comisiones`) the lines' net and exempt values added up and their VAT, which is the VAT rate by the total net value rounded once (the SII's validation 38 for settlement invoices) or the sum of the lines' VAT when a line states its own, and take them off `totalAmount` (Formato DTE 2.5, field 124), which on a 43 may be zero or negative, as may its net, exempt amount and VAT; explicit `totals` are written as given. A 43 is held to what its root `Liquidacion` declares: `createDocument` refuses `transport`, `globalAdjustments`, line discounts and surcharges, a reference's `otherRut`, `totals.nonBillableAmount` and the options `noDebitReduction`, `dispatchType`, `transferType`, `printFormat`, `exportPaymentTerms` and `netAmountsIndicator` (`INVALID_OPTION`), requires the receiver's `businessActivity` (`MISSING_FIELD`) and admits 60 lines and 20 commissions; `settledDocumentType` (`TpoDocLiq`) is required on its lines and refused on any other type. A receipt (39, 41) is held to its own schema, `EnvioBOLETA_v11.xsd`, much shorter than the invoice's: `createDocument` refuses `transport`, `commissions`, `withholdVat: true`, every `options` field but `serviceIndicator`, `netAmountsIndicator` (only 2), `billingPeriod`, `dueDate` and `paymentMedium`, the totals `vatRate`, `ownVatAmount`, `thirdPartyVatAmount`, `withholdings` and `commissions`, and on a line `referenceQuantity`, `referenceUnit`, `referencePrice`, `additionalTaxCodes` and an `exemptIndicator` other than 1, 2 or 6 (`INVALID_OPTION` with the field in `details.field`); it keeps `globalAdjustments`, `subtotals` and `receiptReferences`; the issuer's `branch`, `phone`, `email`, `activityCode` and `salespersonCode` and the receiver's `businessActivity`, which a receipt has no element for, are left out, not refused, so one issuer serves invoices and receipts, and so are the receiver's `email` and postal address, which its schema declares and dte-sdk does not write yet; `totals.periodAmount` is written as the receipt's `TotalPeriodo` (`MontoPeriodo` on other types); `softwareProviderRut` (`RUTProvSW`, the RUT of the provider of the issuing software, the issuer's own for in-house software) is optional, written only when given, and with `options.netAmountsIndicator` (`IndMntNeto`) is refused on every type that is not a receipt. On a receipt `paymentMedium` must be a number from 1 to 5 as text; that is not checked yet. An export document (110, 111, 112) is written under its own root, `Exportaciones`: `currency` (`TpoMoneda`, one of `CURRENCIES`) is required, the receiver is abroad under `FOREIGN_RECEIVER_RUT` (55555555-5) with `receiver.foreign` (`Extranjero`), the customs area goes in `transport.customs` (`Aduana`: sale modality, clause and total, route, ports, weights with their units, `packages` with their marks, freight and insurance, countries), the amounts have four decimals, and so has the share of a line discount or surcharge in percent, which is written as `DescuentoMonto` or `RecargoMonto` only when it is whole and otherwise goes as its percent alone, listed in `warnings` (`calculateExportLineAmount`), unless the line has `wholeShares`, which rounds the share once to a whole number, writes it beside its percent and works the line's amount out with it (5 % of 200 984 is written 10 049, and the line 190 935), a global adjustment given as an amount carries its value in pesos (`ValorDROtrMnda`) when the document brings its `exchangeRate`, the totals are the exempt amount and the same total, zero when `exportPaymentTerms` is 21 (`calculateExportTotals`, through `calculateTotals`), `exchangeRate` adds the totals in pesos (`OtraMoneda`, `PESO CL`, each `convertToPesos`: exact, half away from zero to a whole peso), and the stamp carries the total as written; `createDocument` refuses what `Exportaciones` does not declare (VAT-included prices, withholding, commissions, six `IdDoc` options, every other total, the trailer plate and the departure and arrival, a line's withholding agent and additional taxes, a service indicator outside 3 to 6, a global adjustment without `exemptIndicator` 1, another receiver RUT) and, on a 110, asks what Formato DTE 2.5 asks (the receiver's city and country, each weight's unit, and unless the service indicator excuses them the sale modality, clause and total, the route and each line's quantity and unit, and besides `options.settlementDate` when `exportPaymentTerms` is 32, an advance payment, and the `marks` of each package that is not a container, types 73 to 76 and 78); the customs codes are not checked against the customs tables, which `dte-sdk/catalogs` carries. Before stamping, `createDocument` also refuses what the SII rejects in the content, stopping at the first fault: more than 60 `items`, or 1,000 on a receipt (`INVALID_OPTION`); on every type but a receipt an issuer without `activityCode` (`Acteco`) or an informative subtotal without `description` (`GlosaSTI`) (`MISSING_FIELD`); a line amount or a net, exempt, VAT or total amount that is not a whole number, or is negative outside a 43 (`INVALID_AMOUNT`); a line discount or surcharge in percent above 100 on a receipt, whose schema stops there (`INVALID_AMOUNT`); a given `amount` on a line with a price that is not the price by the quantity less the discount plus the surcharge, nor, on a dispatch guide whose `transferType` is not 1, a zero on a line with no percent (Formato DTE 2.5, field 38 of the detail; `TOTAL_MISMATCH` with `items[i].amount`, `expected` and `actual`); a line that is not a sale (`IndExe` 4 or 5) and every line of a credit note (61, 112) with a reference of `code` 2, which the same field makes zero, are written with an amount of zero whatever their price, refusing another given amount (`TOTAL_MISMATCH`, `expected` 0) and a percent (`INVALID_AMOUNT`), and such a credit note refuses `globalAdjustments` and `commissions` (`INVALID_OPTION`); a unit price of zero is left out, the line written as one with no price (field 22; `PrcItem` starts at 0.000001), and a negative one is refused (`INVALID_AMOUNT`, `items[i].unitPrice`); a quantity, reference quantity or reference price at or below zero (`INVALID_AMOUNT`, `items[i].quantity`, `items[i].referenceQuantity`, `items[i].referencePrice`); a `unitPriceDecimals` below the decimals of the price (`INVALID_OPTION`); a credit note (61, 112) with a reference of `code` 1 or 2, or a debit note (56, 111) with one of `code` 1, and another document reference besides a `SET` one (the `CodRef` row: "un único documento de referencia"; `INVALID_OPTION` on that `references[i]`); a credit note or a debit note (56, 61, 111, 112) with no reference to the document it changes, the `SET` reference of a certification set alone included, since Formato DTE 2.5 makes the reference zone mandatory on both (`MISSING_FIELD`, `references`); a global discount or surcharge whose `value` is not above zero once rounded to its two decimals (`INVALID_AMOUNT`, `globalAdjustments[i].value`; its `kind` says whether it takes off or adds, never the sign of its value) and more than 20 of them (`INVALID_OPTION`, `globalAdjustments`), as `DTE_v10.xsd` and `EnvioBOLETA_v11.xsd` type `ValorDR` and repeat `DscRcgGlobal`; a 33 without `totals.vatAmount` (the SII's validation 55) and a 34 without an exempt amount above zero or with a net amount or VAT (validation 57); and a `totalAmount` that is not net + exempt + VAT + the deposit guarantee less the VAT withheld (code 15) and the commissions, or a `periodAmount` that is not the total plus the non-billable amount (`TOTAL_MISMATCH` with `expected` and `actual`; a total whose totals carry another tax code is not checked). What the SII accepts with an objection is built and listed in `document.warnings` (`DocumentWarning`: validation 10, a total of zero on a 33, 34, 43 or 46; 12, a net amount of zero on a 33, 43 or 46; 56, a 33 whose net amount is not above zero), never written to the XML. A 39 issued without `pricesIncludeVat` whose totals carry a net amount gets `IndMntNeto` 2 by itself. `createEnvelope` admits 2,000 documents in an `EnvioDTE` and 500 in an `EnvioBOLETA` (`INVALID_OPTION`, `documents`). Its `cover.setId`, like the `id` of `createPurchaseSalesBook`, `createGuideBook` and `createFolioConsumption`, is an `xs:ID` in the SII's schemas: one that is not a letter or an underscore followed by letters, digits, full stops, hyphens and underscores is refused (`INVALID_OPTION`, `cover.setId` or `id`), and so is a `cover.setId` that is the id of a document of the envelope; an id left out is generated. `toSiiDocument`/`fromSiiDocument` map the English model (`totalAmount`, `issuer.businessName`) to the official SII tags (`MntTotal`, `RznSoc`) in schema order. `stampDocument` builds the exact `<DD>` string and signs it with the CAF private key (SHA1withRSA over ISO-8859-1 bytes). `signDocument` applies the enveloped XMLDSig signature (C14N 1.0, RSA-SHA1) the SII validates. `createEnvelope`/`signEnvelope` produce `EnvioDTE`/`EnvioBOLETA`. Certificates load from PKCS#12 or PEM; CAF files are parsed and checked for range and the 6-month expiry of invoice/note CAFs. `verifyReceivedDocuments(xml, { environment?, siiKeys?, trustedCertificates? })` checks a `DTE`, `EnvioDTE` or `EnvioBOLETA` as received, each document read from its element: the envelope's own signature and, per document, its XMLDSig signature, its TED (`FRMT` with the key of the CAF the TED carries, `DD` against the header), that CAF against the document (issuer, type, folio inside the range) and the SII's `FRMA` over the CAF with the key of its `IDK` (`SII_CAF_KEYS`: 100 certification, 300 production; only the key of `environment`, production by default, is accepted, and a CAF of the other environment is invalid; `verifyCafSignature` checks one CAF, an empty `FRMA` is `invalid`, and `cafEnvironment` reads the environment of an `IDK`); each check is data with a `status` of `valid`, `invalid` or `unchecked` (no key for that `IDK`), and malformed input throws. With `trustedCertificates`, the certificates of the certification authorities the caller trusts as PEM or DER, each signature that verifies also reports its `signer` (`rut`, `name`, `notBefore`, `notAfter` and `inForceWhenSigned`, against the instant the signed element states) when one of them issued the certificate it verifies with, or is that certificate, and `null` otherwise; the RUT is the person's who holds the certificate, no revocation is looked up, and a signature that verifies alone says nothing of who signed. `createReceptionAnswer`, `createResultAnswer` and `createGoodsReceipts` answer a received `EnvioDTE` document by document, each signed and on its own (the `RespuestaDTE` with `RecepcionEnvio`/`RecepcionDTE`, the `RespuestaDTE` with `ResultadoDTE`, and the `EnvioRecibos` of Ley 19.983): they take the envelope as received or read with `readReceivedEnvelope`, which reads it as `verifyReceivedDocuments` does (an `EnvioDTE` or `EnvioBOLETA` with no DOCTYPE, one `SetDTE` with every `DTE` directly inside it, and each document giving its own type, folio, date, issuer, receiver and total; nothing is taken from the cover and no number is converted, and a document that lacks a field refuses the envelope with `XML_PARSE_FAILED`), and decide each document's state and gloss through a function or a record keyed by `documentKey` (`'33:1234'`; `null` leaves it out; a record is refused with `INVALID_OPTION` when two documents of the envelope share a type and a folio, or when one of its keys names no document of the envelope). The reception answer quotes the digest of the envelope's own signature (`Digest`, read as `ReceivedEnvelope.digest`). Only the reception answer has defaults (another RUT is `EstadoRecepDTE` 3, any other 0): `documents` is required in the commercial result and in the receipts, which accept, reject and receipt nothing the caller did not decide (a document without a decision is left out, and a rejection without a code writes `CodRchDsc` -1). The codes are in `ENVELOPE_RECEPTION_STATES` (`EstadoRecepEnv`), `DOCUMENT_RECEPTION_STATES` (`EstadoRecepDTE`) and `COMMERCIAL_RESULT_STATES` (`EstadoDTE`); `createExchangeAnswers` of `dte-sdk/portal` is built on the same answers, and `parseExchangeSet` reads the SII's own set loosely. `unstable_createAssignment` builds and signs, with no network, the electronic assignment file (AEC, Formato Archivo Electrónico de Cesión 1.1, `AEC_v10.xsd`) with which the creditor of a 33, 34, 46 or 43 (`ASSIGNABLE_DOCUMENT_TYPES`) assigns it under Ley 19.983: the signed `DTE` embedded verbatim in a signed `DocumentoDTECedido`, the `DocumentoCesion` (`SeqCesion` 1) signed by each of one to three authorized signers with their own certificate, and the whole file signed as `DocumentoAEC`, with the sworn statement (`DeclaracionJurada`) the format words when no electronic receipt is carried; it refuses a document whose signature does not verify (`SIGNATURE_INVALID`), a first assignment by anyone but the creditor, an amount outside 1 to the total and texts past the stricter of the format's and the schema's lengths. `unstable_createReassignment({ previous, ... })` adds the next assignment, by the previous assignee, to an earlier file whose signatures all verify, up to 40 (`MAX_ASSIGNMENTS`), and `unstable_verifyAssignment` checks every signature of a file where it stands; the three carry the `unstable_` prefix until a file they built is registered at the SII. Its `receipts` carries the debtor's electronic receipts, given as the `EnvioRecibos` files the debtor sent or as lone `Recibo` elements: each one that names the document is carried as it was signed, verified, up to 40, and with them the file carries no sworn statement; `documentImage` and `receiptImage` carry the document and the receipts that are not electronic as PDFs (`ImagenDTE`, `ImagenAR`), and `unstable_verifyAssignment` verifies each receipt too. Status codes from the SII web services are classified (`accepted`, `pending`, `rejected`, `queryError`). A line's `withholdingAgent` writes `Retenedor`, the element of a transaction of a withholding agent (`{}` marks it with `IndAgente` R; `slaughterBase`, `marginBase` and `finalConsumerPrice` are `MntBaseFaena`, `MntMargComer` and `PrcConsFinal`); a receipt and a settlement invoice refuse it. Signatures are RSA-SHA1, PKCS#1 v1.5, so they are deterministic: the first one of the process is worked out by the runtime's own RSA (Node, Bun, Deno) and by the JavaScript engine and compared, and only when they agree does the runtime sign the ones that follow; `rsaSigningEngine()` says which signs (`native`, `portable`, or null before the first). Errors are `DteError` with stable codes and no personal data in messages. All clock-dependent functions accept `{ now }`.

The SII web services client is `createSiiClient({ environment, certificate, companyRut })` plus free functions: `uploadEnvelope`/`uploadBook`/`uploadFolioConsumption` (DTEUpload multipart in ISO-8859-1, or the receipts REST API in production; the XML must open with a declaration naming ISO-8859-1; duplicates return the original TrackID), `queryUploadStatus`/`waitForUploadStatus`/`queryDocumentStatus`/`folioReceived`, the acceptance/claim registry `registerClaim`/`listClaimEvents`/`queryTransferable`/`queryReceptionDate`/`receiverStatus` (for types `CLAIM_DOCUMENT_TYPES`, 33, 34 and 43, with the guard `isClaimDocumentType`), the pure `receiverAnswer` (the whole `listClaimEvents` result plus reception date plus today: annulled, claimed, accepted, `paidInCash` when the SII marked it paid in cash (`PAG`; the registry refuses events on it with code 27 and there is no deadline), tacitly accepted after 8 calendar days, goods received, pending, or `unknown` when the query failed with no events, and the claim deadline), `unstable_uploadAssignment` (an AEC to the registry of credit transfers, `RTCAnotEnvio.cgi`, with the notification address and the assignor's RUT, held to the file's `RutCedente`; any `STATUS` but 0 is `SII_UPLOAD_REJECTED`) and `unstable_queryAssignmentUploadStatus` (`getEstEnvio` of `wsRPETCConsulta`, its codes returned unclassified), both unstable because they have not run against the SII and the format does not describe the registry's services, and `queryAuthorizedIssuer`, the public registry of authorized issuers (resolution number and date of the environment, document types; no certificate or session needed). Tokens are obtained and renewed automatically per environment, channel and certificate. Transport is injectable (`fetch` by default, `createNodeHttpsTransport` from `dte-sdk/node` with TLS verification on; `tls.ca` adds to Node's bundled roots), retries use exponential backoff and never re-send an upload or a claim after an SII answer (not even a partial one), and `capture`/`archive` ports record redacted HTTP exchanges and the bytes of every upload. The `status` of `queryUploadStatus` is the verdict of the upload, not the class of its code: the SII answers `EPR` once the envelope is processed, whatever it did with each document, so with rejected documents in the counts it is `partiallyRejected` (or `rejected` when none was accepted) and with objections alone `acceptedWithObjections`; `counts` adds up every document type, `countsByType` has each, and `uploadVerdict(cls, counts)` is the same rule as a pure function. `classifyUploadStatus` still reads a code alone. The counts are the SII's, type by type, and may cover fewer documents than the envelope carried, of which the verdict then says nothing: given `documents`, the number of documents of the envelope, `queryUploadStatus` and `waitForUploadStatus` say in `unreported` how many the counts leave out (null without `documents` or without counts), each to be asked for with `queryDocumentStatus`, which takes no export document (110, 111, 112: `INVALID_DOCUMENT_TYPE`). The receipt of an upload carries `retryAfterMs`, the wait the SII's receipts REST API asks for in its `X-Retry-After` header before the status is asked, in milliseconds, or null when the answer names none; passed to `waitForUploadStatus` as `initialDelayMs`, it is waited before the first poll, cut to one hour, and `timeoutMs` counts from that poll. When the SII refuses a file sent through DTEUpload, `SII_UPLOAD_REJECTED` carries in `details.body` the first 2,000 characters of its reply, redacted, for a reply with no `DETAIL/ERROR` line to read in `errors`.

The catalogs are typed constants of the root entry. Beyond `DOCUMENT_TYPES`, `REFERENCE_CODES`, `TRANSFER_TYPES`, `DISPATCH_TYPES`, `SERVICE_INDICATORS`, `PAYMENT_TERMS`, `EXEMPT_INDICATORS` and the books' codes, they hold, each with a type guard, the tables of Formato DTE 2.5 and of the receipts' format: `ADDITIONAL_TAXES` (the 40 codes `TipoImp` and `CodImpAdic` take, by code, each with its SII `name`, its `kind` (`additional`, `specific`, `margin`, `advance` or `withholding`), the `rate` the table gives, the electronic `documents` it applies to and the `totalWithholdingCode` that takes its place when the buyer withholds the whole VAT; `isAdditionalTaxCode`; the schema also admits 16, 40, 54 and 55, which the table does not describe and are left out), `PAYMENT_MEDIA` (`MedioPago`: `CH`, `CF`, `LT`, `EF`, `PE`, `TC`, `OT`; `isPaymentMedium`), `RECEIPT_PAYMENT_MEDIA` (a receipt's `MedioPago`, `'1'` to `'5'` as `paymentMedium` carries them; `isReceiptPaymentMedium`), `REFERENCE_DOCUMENT_TYPES` (the 42 numeric `TpoDocRef` codes with their names; an alphabetic one such as `SET` is not checked; `isReferenceDocumentType`) and `RECEIPT_REFERENCE_DOCUMENT_TYPES` (the 11 a receipt's reference can name; `isReceiptReferenceDocumentType`). They are data: `createDocument` does not check a document against them. The units of measure (`UnmdItem`, `UnmdRef`) have no table: they are free text the SII does not check outside exports. The business activities (`Acteco`) come from `dte-sdk/catalogs`: `BUSINESS_ACTIVITIES` holds the 674 codes of the SII's list of economic activity codes, sorted, each with its `name` and the list's columns as the SII writes them, `subjectToVat` ("Afecto a IVA": `SI`, `NO`, or `G`, decided by the activity's own characteristics), `taxCategory` (`1`, `2` or `G`) and `availableOnline` ("Disponible Internet"); `businessActivity(code)` looks one up and `isBusinessActivityCode` is its guard. A code the list writes with a leading zero, such as `011101`, is the number 11101.

The SII books are `createPurchaseSalesBook` (IECV, `LibroCompraVenta`), `createGuideBook` (`LibroGuia`) and `createFolioConsumption` (RCOF, `ConsumoFolios`), each with `build*Xml`, `sign*`, `verify*Signature` and `toSii*`. All submission kinds of the schemas are covered, and the SDK computes the summaries from the lines; `summaryOnlyTotals` and `previousTotals` carry what cannot be derived. An explicit line total that differs from the SII formula is kept and reported in `totalMismatches`, and `strictTotals: true` throws `BOOK_TOTAL_MISMATCH` instead. `bookEntryFromDocument`, `guideEntryFromDocument` and `folioConsumptionEntryFromDocument` derive the lines from issued documents; `bookEntryFromDocument` carries a deposit guarantee as `containerDeposit` (`DepEnvase`) and refuses `creditNoteSign: 'negative'` on a credit note that has one (`INVALID_OPTION`, `creditNoteSign`). The folio consumption report takes the three types `ConsumoFolio_v10.xsd` admits in a summary: the receipt (39), the exempt receipt (41) and the credit note (61), which is reported after the receipts with its net, its VAT and its exempt amount, and its folios counted, used and voided; `folioConsumptionEntryFromDocument` derives the line of a receipt alone (`INVALID_DOCUMENT_TYPE` for a 61), so the line of a credit note is given as a `FolioConsumptionEntry` built by hand. The signed XML goes to `uploadBook` or `uploadFolioConsumption`. The RCV replaced the IECV in production from period 2017-08, the guide book is sent only on SII request, and the report is used in the receipts certification; the SII probably no longer requires it in production. The VAT a purchase invoice (45, 46) withholds comes off the line total on both sides, in each side's own fields: `totalVatWithheld`/`partialVatWithheld` (`IVARetTotal`, `IVARetParcial`) on a sale line, and `otherTaxes` under a withholding code, 15 with the rate of the tax when the whole VAT was withheld, on a purchase line, which is refused with `INVALID_OPTION` if it brings either of the sale line's two fields; `bookEntryFromDocument` follows its `operation`.

Certification (deterministic half, from `dte-sdk/portal`): `parseTestSetText` parses the SII test-set text into sets and cases; `planCertificationSets` gives what each set issues and the folios per type; `createFolioAllocator` hands out folios with the CAF that stamps them; `issueTestSet` issues the basic, exempt, guide and purchase sets through phase 1 with the `SET` reference (`CASO <id>`) and the field rules, written in a fixed form (the issue date on the Chile day, as the SII's instructions for the test set ask, and UTC stamps with milliseconds, unit prices with six decimals, zero totals on the notes that correct a text), naming `receiver` or, with `receivers`, several customers in turn on its invoices and guides, and the settlement set when the text holds it (`SET LIQUIDACION FACTURA`, asked for on download as `SET84`): one settlement invoice (43) per case in one envelope, each item a line with its quantity and its `TOTAL LINEA` as the signed amount, the settled document type (`TpoDocLiq`) from the item name (99 for an advance or any other transaction, else the electronic or paper code of an invoice, note, receipt or earlier settlement), exempt when the name starts with `EXENTO`, its commissions and other charges taken off the total, their VAT rounded once over their net total, and its VAT split in own and third-party (`splitVat`: `IVAProp`, `IVATerc`); the runner sends, declares and awaits it with the other sets (the grammar rests on synthetic sets: the SII hands the real one out per company); and the two export sets when the text holds them, each with its attention number and in its own envelope (`envio-set-exportacion-1.xml`, `-2.xml`): the export invoices (110), the credit note (112) and the debit note (111) of its cases, each exempt and in the currency of its case, the freight and the insurance in the customs area and as two global surcharges, a commission stated as a percent of the sale clause as a third, the names the set gives in words (ports, countries, clauses, units, packages) as the codes of the customs tables, a line with a discount written with `wholeShares`, every package with the marks `S/M`, and an invoice that names no sale modality as a service, lodging when its item says so; what the text does not give comes in `exportSets` (`ExportSetOptions`): `exchangeRates`, the pesos per unit of each currency by the name the set gives it, with no default (a currency without one stops the set before a folio is taken), `receiver`, the foreign customer (`DEFAULT_CERTIFICATION_FOREIGN_RECEIVER` for what it leaves out), `tarePercent`, the tare as a percent of the net weight (2 by default), and `containerId` and `seal` for a case whose package is a container (a stand-in each by default); `checkExportSets` works every document of those sets out before the run asks for folios, and a currency the SII does not list is refused there (`INVALID_OPTION`, `currency`); `issueSimulation` re-issues every case in one envelope, the settlement invoices and the documents of the export sets included, and `simulationFolioNeeds` counts their folios; `createCertificationSalesBook`, `createCertificationPurchaseBook` and `createCertificationGuideBook` build and sign the books through phase 3, as total submissions or adjustments, with fixed lines and summaries (the whole VAT a purchase invoice withholds as another tax with code 15 and rate 19, off its total, and the common-use credit rounded per document). Nothing sends: the runner does.

Certification (portal half, from `dte-sdk/portal`): `runCertification` runs the HTML side in the field's order from a `CertificationStore` (`createMemoryCertificationStore`, `createDirectoryCertificationStore`; the state holds CAF private keys): the test sets, the books, the simulation, the exchange set answered on the exchange portal (`downloadExchangeSet`, `validateExchangeUser`, `uploadExchangeAnswers`, `confirmExchange`; the answers from `createExchangeAnswers`, signed and schema-valid), the printed samples uploaded to the samples portal when the `samples` option gives them (`readPrintedSamples` from `dte-sdk/pdf`; `readSamplesReview`, `createSamplesReview`, `uploadSample`, `submitSamplesReview`, `readSamplesDetail`), and the declaration of compliance, irreversible, only with `declareCompliance: true`; it stops with `exchange` (the set unavailable or the company not in the exchange), `printedSamples` (no samples given), `rejected` (the SII's reasons in the detail) or `compliance`. Each phase is a step over the dependencies and the state (`obtainTestSet`, `prepareFolios`, `sendTestSet`, `declareTestSets`, `waitForTestSetsApproval`, `runBooks`, `advanceToNextStage`, `sendSimulation`, `declareSimulation`, `waitForSimulationApproval`, `runExchange`, `uploadPrintedSamples`, `declareComplianceFinal`), with typed progress events through `onProgress`, and `beforeUpload`, handed each file the run is about to upload (a test set, the simulation, a book) after it is kept as an artefact, where a check that throws stops the step with nothing sent, the place to hold the file against the SII's schema with `validateAgainstSchema`; beneath them the portal operations `downloadTestSet` (generates the set anew at the SII), `declareProgress` (every field in form order, the page read again to verify), `readProgress`, `advanceStage`, `listBookHistory` and `declareCompliance`. The two GWT portals speak GWT-RPC (`gwtBody`, `gwtAnswer`); the exchange uses the pair of hashes known to work and the samples portal's are discovered once with that pair as the fallback. Each portal is entered once per stage of work (`withExchangeStage`, `withSamplesStage`; the operations take `stage`), its calls are sent once with no time-out of their own and a fixed set of headers, their answers read as UTF-8; any failure of the set download asks for the set by hand, and the set is read loosely. The run keeps to field behaviour in what the SII receives and in how it flows: the declaration carries today's Chile date, the uploads of the run retry only network failures (eight attempts) and take `STATUS` 99 as a failed send, a portal request waits 20 s, and `receiver` and the issuer's activity, commune and city have defaults (`DEFAULT_CERTIFICATION_RECEIVER`, `DEFAULT_CERTIFICATION_ISSUER`). The cover of every envelope names the company's resolution in the certification environment, and the SII refuses an envelope that names another: given no `resolution.date`, `runCertification` reads the date the portal shows for the company (`fetchCompanyResolution`) at the stages that still send an envelope, and when the portal shows none, or a page that cannot be read, goes on with the day's UTC date and a warning in the portal client's logger; the number is the one given, or 0, and a step run on its own keeps number 0 and the day's date. The rows the progress page gives the export sets have not been seen: they are looked for as `SET` … `EXPORT` in one label, and an export set that was sent and whose row the page does not show, or shows with no state, is not taken as approved, so the wait ends `timedOut` with a `detail` that names it; a caller who sees the sets approved goes on by saving the state with `setsApproved: true` and `stage: 'books'`. The books phase starts over on every run (the period from the UTC month the set was read in, the approved books from the portal), resends as adjustments or in the next free period, and never stops on a portal read; with the three mandatory books sent the runner asks for the next stage and stops with the portal's sentence when it does not move (`runBooks` is `incomplete` only when a mandatory book could not be sent; `advanceToNextStage` returns `advanced`, `unchanged`, `failed` or `timedOut` and never throws for a portal answer). The simulation carries the local date of the process and UTC stamps to the second; the declaration of compliance counts as made when the last page no longer shows its form. Before issuing, the run asks the SII (as the company) whether it already holds the folios it is about to use, uses a range obtained again only through the folios the SII showed free, reads a maximum it cannot read as no cap, never asks for a blocked type and keeps the annulled ranges in the state. The waits are the field's and `sleep` and `now` are injectable. None of it has been run against the portal yet.

Certification of receipts (from `dte-sdk/portal`), an application of its own with no runner, as pieces to chain, kept to field behaviour like the document runner (the set read by position, the UTC day and UTC stamps to the second on the receipts, uploads read and retried as the run's, the portal called with a fixed set of headers, once, 30 s, UTF-8, its states searched in the raw answer; `sendReceiptsSet().envelopeTrackId` is null for a duplicate without a track id): `downloadReceiptsTestSet` (the plain-text set), `parseReceiptsTestSet`, `issueReceiptsSet` (one receipt of type 39 per case to the final consumer, prices with VAT, the reference `SET` / `CASO-<n>`, the signed `EnvioBOLETA`), `sendReceiptsSet` (uploads the envelope, waits 20 s, reads its status, then sends the folio consumption report with the sequence number 100 plus the attempt, up to ten attempts; `sent` unless the envelope is rejected, `envelopeRejected`, or the report cannot be uploaded or is refused for lack of authorisation, `consumptionFailed`), `declareReceiptsTrackId`, then later `readReceiptsStatus` (`readyToDeclare` at `P90`, `declared` at `P91`) and `declareReceiptsCompliance` (irreversible; `provider` is mandatory; the representative is the owner of the session; `alreadyDeclared` and `notReady` are outcomes), and `verifyReceiptsAuthorization` (type 39 among the stamping types of a production client, and the receipts row of the certification progress page; never throws, a form not served is `queryFailed`). A receipt (39, 41) takes `receiptReferences` (`code`, `reason`, optional `documentType` and `folio`), never `references`: the receipts schema has its own `Referencia`, without a date. None of it has been run against the receipts portal yet.

Printed samples (Node only, from `dte-sdk/pdf`): `parsePrintableDocuments` turns any `EnvioDTE`, `EnvioBOLETA`, bare `SetDTE` or bare `DTE` XML, given as text or as the bytes of its file (UTF-8 when they are UTF-8, ISO-8859-1 otherwise), into printable documents with each `TED` as it was signed (as written when its `FRMT` verifies over its `DD` with the key of the CAF it carries, otherwise the form the `FRMT` does verify, without the whitespace between its tags or with its `DD` written again, as in a file indented after signing; as written when none verifies); `renderPrintedSample` draws one PDF per the SII printed-samples manual (21.5 cm wide, each page 11 to 33 cm tall; a document taller than 33 cm goes on to further pages, each repeating the issuer, the type box and the SII office with `Página n de m` under it, the date and the receiver on the first only, a table's column head repeated where it breaks, and the totals, acknowledgement box, stamp and `CEDIBLE` mark on the last with at least the last detail line, every page but the last 33 cm tall; one page when it fits, with no page number; red type box, a guide's transfer type, the transport area of a guide or an invoice that moves goods with what its `Transporte` carries in the order of Formato DTE 2.5 (both plates, the carrier's RUT, the driver's name and RUT, the destination's address, commune and city, the departure date and time and the arrival date; what the document lacks is left out, and the parsed document carries it as `transport`, a `PrintableTransport`), the commissions and other charges of a settlement invoice (43) or a purchase invoice and its notes listed under the detail with their description, rate and values and taken off in the totals, the additional taxes and withholdings of `ImptoReten` in the totals by the name Formato DTE 2.5 gives each code with their rate, the VAT withholdings with a minus, and the VAT not withheld, every amount as the document carries it (`commissions`, `withholdings` and the totals of `parsePrintableDocuments`), what Formato DTE 2.5 marks to be printed when the document has it (the payment terms in words and the due date under the issue date, an item's additional description under its name, the special credit of construction companies among the totals with a minus), dates with the month in words, who dispatches the goods in words, the city of each party when it is not the commune again, the receiver's RUT with dots, a referenced document that is not a DTE by the name of its code and `CodRef` in words before the reason, quantities and unit prices the Chilean way with up to six decimals, the total in words (`Son: …`), `SIN TIMBRE ELECTRÓNICO` in a box in place of the stamp on a document with no `TED` (`paymentTerms`, `dueDate`, `dispatchType`, `city`, an item's `description`, a reference's `code` and `totals.constructionCredit` of `parsePrintableDocuments`), and the rest of the format's print column when the document has it (under the issue date the payment medium and the kind of account in words, the account number, the bank, the terms of payment, the amount paid, the balance owed and each scheduled payment; under the receiver the kind of special invoice, who issues a guide for export in words and its authorising resolution, the principal's and the requester's RUT; in the receiver's box the document of a foreign receiver; among the totals the bases of meat slaughter and of trade margins, the deposit guarantee and, under them, the totals in another currency; under an item its surcharge, a withholding agent's bases and price to the final consumer and its value in another currency; a global adjustment's description; read into the optional fields of `PrintableDocument`, `PrintablePayment`, `PrintableReceiver` and `PrintableOtherCurrency`), an export document (110, 111, 112) with its amounts in the currency it names (a `Moneda` row, the decimals each amount has, no peso sign and no total in words), its payment terms in words and its customs area in the transport box, each code by the name its customs table gives it and one the table does not list as written (`transport.customs`, `currency` and `exportPaymentTerms` of `parsePrintableDocuments`; a dispatch guide prints the customs area it carries the same way), an item code wider than its column wrapped inside it, acknowledgement box and `CEDIBLE` mark on the transferable copy of 33, 34, 43, 46 and sale guides, PDF417 stamp with the signed bytes and its legends; `paper: 'roll'` prints it on continuous paper 80 mm wide, as tall as its content, for any type but an export document (`INVALID_OPTION`, `paper`), and `stamp: false` leaves the stamp out of a receipt, 39 or 41, as Res. Ex. SII N° 207 of 2025 allows, and throws `INVALID_OPTION` on any other type; the resolution line under the stamp is the `resolution` option, a string printed as given or the company's resolution as `{ number, date }` (`NroResol`, and `FchResol` as `YYYY-MM-DD`) printed as `Res. Ex. SII N° {number} del {year}`, and by default number 0 of the clock's year); `resolutionLine` gives that line alone; `verificationSite` names the site of the legend under the stamp, `www.sii.cl` by default; the SII office under the type box is `siiOffice` or the one of the issuer's commune, matched by its letters and digits alone, and none when the table does not know the commune; `renderTedBarcode` gives the stamp PNG alone; `renderPrintedSamples` batches envelopes in memory into the test and simulation sets with failures as data; `writePrintedSamples` and `findEnvelopeFiles` do the same over files (`SET-PRUEBAS`, `SET-SIMULACION`). `pdf-lib` and `bwip-js` load on first use. The stamp is always at error correction level 5, and one with a byte above ASCII (a name in another issuer's document) is written in byte compaction alone when it fits. The sheet draws the stamp section A.2.5 of the SII's instructions describes (`'instructions'`): eighteen data columns, 387 modules across and 9 cm wide, rows three modules high, bytes alone whenever the TED fits, one factor for its two sides and a quarter of an inch clear above and below it. `unstable_stampGeometry: 'compact'` of `renderPrintedSample` keeps on the sheet the stamp of every release up to 0.16.0, rows one module high stretched to the stamp box; that one is the stamp of the continuous paper, which refuses `'instructions'` (`INVALID_OPTION`, `unstable_stampGeometry`), and the one `renderTedBarcode` draws unless its `unstable_geometry` asks for the other. The option keeps its `unstable_` name because no stamp drawn as `'instructions'` has been printed and read back with a scanner.

The SII portal, from `dte-sdk/portal`, is `createPortalClient({ environment, certificate, companyRut })` plus free functions, on Node (client certificate over `https`; TLS 1.2, server verified). The certificate must be enabled as a login method at sii.cl, or the login throws `SII_PORTAL_CERT_NOT_ENABLED`. Session: `openPortalSession`, `closePortalSession`, or on demand; `sessionCache` and `lock` are ports for several replicas. Company data: `fetchCompanyResolution` (per environment), `fetchTaxpayerData`, `fetchIssuerProfile`, `queryCertificationSets`. Folios: `listStampableTypes`, `queryFolioQuota` (`MAX_AUTOR`, `FOLIOS_DISP`; stamps nothing), `requestCaf` (may grant less than asked; read `granted`), `listFolioRanges`, `annulFolios` (explicit scope required; `maxRanges` limits one call; irreversible; counts against the quota for six months), `listReobtainableRanges`, `reobtainCaf` (signs in on demand; a login page in answer is `SII_PORTAL_SESSION_EXPIRED`). Composite flows return refusals as data: `requestCafExact`, `requestCafInBatches`, `reobtainFolios`. Once a folio flow holds something (CAFs, or folios the SII annulled), any other `DteError` of a later step comes back as data too, in `failure: { code, operation, rejection? }`, and is logged redacted: `requestCafInBatches` and `reobtainFolios` return their CAFs, `annulFolios` and `requestCafExact` their `knownAnnulled`; persist `knownAnnulled` either way; a range its keys cover, in one key or several, is not posted again. A refusal after a grant keeps its kind; only `quotaExceeded` reads as `quotaCapReached`. `portalMessage` is redacted. Refusals are `SII_PORTAL_REJECTED` with `details.rejection` and `portalRejectionMessage`. `createFolioRegistry`, `createMemoryFolioRegistry` and `createDirectoryFolioRegistry` (owner-only `folios.json`) track folios locally. The CAF XML holds a private key: treat it as a secret. `unstable_replenishFolios` (unstable: its shape may change in any release; not run against the SII yet, in either environment) keeps a type stocked in one call: below `minimum` usable folios it downloads again the authorized ranges nobody holds, requests what is missing in batches and annuls as a last resort (certification only unless `allowAnnul`; never a CAF held or a range the run downloaded; only when `FOLIOS_DISP` is over the folios in hand; ranges of the last 180 days). It needs `cafs` (every CAF held, with its unused folios) and `lastIssuedFolio`, stores nothing, returns `status` (`none`, `coolDown`, `replenished`, `partial`, `blocked`, `failed`) with `cafs`, and `coolUntil` and `knownAnnulled` to pass back, and hands what it obtains to `onObtained` with the portal lock held. `planFolioReplenishment` is its decision with no I/O; `reason` is the cause (`low`, `exhausted`, `expired`). `unstable_createPasswordPortalClient({ environment, userRut, password, companyRut })` makes a client that signs in with the RUT and the tax password of a person instead of a certificate (`password` is a function, asked for at each login and never kept; the capture writes `clave=[redacted]`; a password the SII refused is never sent again by the same client, whose next login throws `SII_PORTAL_LOGIN_FAILED` with `refusedBefore: true`; the key of its session in `sessionCache` is random and of that client alone, since a cached session is used without the password, unless `sessionKey`, a secret of that person, is given to share it); every portal function takes it, and it is unstable because that login has not been run against the SII by dte-sdk yet. `unstable_fetchExchangeMailbox(portal, { rut })` asks the registry of authorized issuers, with the session, for the mailbox another taxpayer registered for the exchange (`exchangeEmail`, null when none), where the answers to a received document go, with its name, resolution and document types; unstable because the page has not been read against the SII by dte-sdk yet.

The purchase and sales register runs on the portal session: `unstable_downloadRegisterFile(portal, { period, operation, accountingStatus })` gives the official detail of a period as the file of the register's "Descargar Detalles" (`csv`, and `columns` and `rows` as texts; an empty file for a period with no documents; `SII_PORTAL_REJECTED` with `rejection: 'registerFileRefused'` and the SII's `code` when the SII refuses the period; unstable, not run against the SII yet), beside `listPeriodDocuments`, `fetchRegisterSummary`, `listPurchaseTypes`, `fetchPurchaseDocument`. `REGISTER_DOCUMENT_CODES` and `registerDocumentCode(code)` describe the 49 document codes of the register (sides, DTE, sign, per-document, buyer withholds VAT) and `REGISTER_ACCOUNTING_STATUSES` the statuses of each side. Response codes are not looked at, so a refused month reads as empty; rows have typed fields, `null` when absent, and `raw`. Writes on a production client change the real register: `changePurchaseType`, `moveVatToCommonUse`, `moveVatToRecoverable` are one attempt each, confirmed only by the SII's `OK`; on `purchaseChangeNotConfirmed` the change may have applied, so read the document again before retrying, and VAT amounts are final amounts, not a delta. `downloadMipymeBackup` reads the XML from production whatever the client's environment, in pieces of at most 20 documents, newest first, in the result or through `onChunk`. A day that cannot be downloaded throws before any download. Known defect: a two-day range over 20 documents downloads only its first day, while `total` counts both.

The activity verification runs on the portal session too, and reads production whatever the client's environment: `unstable_fetchActivityVerification` (unstable: its shape may change in any release; read once against the real SII, for a pending verification) gives the company's `requests` (number, kind, reason, `preliminaryResult`, `finalResult`, `status`, `statusDescription`, `requestedOn`, `accreditationDeadline`, `procedureStatus`, `hasCertificate`) and the SII's `messages` (`text`, `blocking`), never officials, comments or the address; it sends the company's RUT, and a request of another RUT throws `SII_PORTAL_UNEXPECTED_PAGE` with `step: 'otherTaxpayer'`; an SII error code throws `activityVerificationRefused`. `listAccreditationDocuments` gives the documents the SII takes to accredit an activity (`category` `general` or `specific`, `code`, `description`; codes repeat across categories).

- [rut.ts](https://github.com/arrowsw/rut.ts): the RUT library dte-sdk depends on
